lines: GTA 6 already broke the internet. And it's not even out yet.
The game is 212 gigabytes. And analysts expect 25 million copies sold on day one.
If everyone downloads at midnight, that's 5 billion gigabytes at once. So why won't the internet melt?
Trick one. They already sent it. Pre-load opened nine days early, and gave one British network its busiest day ever.
Trick two. You don't download it from Rockstar. The game is copied onto thousands of servers, so yours comes from one near your city.
Trick three. Time zones. PS5 unlocks at midnight local time, so the wave rolls around the Earth instead of hitting all at once.
So on launch night, almost nothing moves. The game is already on your console, locked. Midnight just turns the key.
Unless there's a day one patch. Then good luck.
Rockstar needed 200 gigabytes of 3D. You need one sketch. Vi3W turns it into a 3D model in seconds.
